belle-isle-aquarium.description: Belle Isle Aquarium is the historic public aquarium beside the Anna Scripps Whitcomb Conservatory, with freshwater and marine exhibits inside its green-tiled gallery.
belle-isle-aquarium.location: Navigate to the named Aquarium/Conservatory complex on Inselruhe Avenue, shortly after entering Belle Isle. The aquarium and conservatory are adjacent but keep different weekly schedules.
belle-isle-aquarium.parking: Use the attraction parking near the Aquarium/Conservatory complex. A Recreation Passport is required for motor vehicles; pedestrians, bicyclists and Route 12 riders do not need one.
belle-isle-aquarium.hours: The aquarium is open Thursday through Sunday, 10:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. It remains open during its current renovation, but construction or holiday notices can alter access.
belle-isle-aquarium.restrooms: Belle Isle Conservancy does not promise a particular aquarium restroom in its visitor information and cautions that some island bathrooms have limited accessibility. Confirm facility access before relying on an indoor restroom.
belle-isle-aquarium.fees: Aquarium admission is free. Driving onto Belle Isle requires a Recreation Passport; parking, food and other island activities can have separate costs.
belle-isle-aquarium.accessibility: The aquarium is open during work intended to improve site drainage, HVAC and accessibility. Construction can change the entrance route, and the Conservancy documents limitations at some island bathrooms; contact the operator for a specific accommodation.
belle-isle-aquarium.dogs: Michigan DNR prohibits pets in park buildings except service animals. Leashed pets may use permitted outdoor park areas but should not be brought into the aquarium.
belle-isle-aquarium.family: The compact fish exhibits make this a practical family stop, especially when paired with the adjacent conservatory. Verify both schedules because the conservatory is open Wednesday through Sunday while the aquarium starts Thursday.
belle-isle-aquarium.need: Do not assume the aquarium follows the island's outdoor hours. It closes at 4:00 p.m., remains under renovation and can develop a wait on busy weekends; confirm the same-day notice before crossing the bridge.

anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.description: Anna Scripps Whitcomb Conservatory is Belle Isle's restored glass-domed botanical conservatory and formal garden complex beside the aquarium.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.location: Use the exact conservatory building pin at the Aquarium/Conservatory complex on Inselruhe Avenue. The two attractions share an arrival zone but have separate entrances and hours.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.parking: Park near the Aquarium/Conservatory complex. Motor vehicles need a Recreation Passport; Route 12 stops at the complex, and a rideshare drop-off is also listed near the aquarium and main entrance.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.hours: The conservatory is open Wednesday through Sunday, 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Holiday, event and maintenance notices can shorten that schedule.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.restrooms: The Conservancy does not identify a guaranteed restroom inside the conservatory and notes limited accessibility at some island bathrooms. Confirm the current facility before a visit that depends on one.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.fees: Ordinary conservatory admission is free. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry, and private events or professional photography require separate arrangements and fees.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.accessibility: Developed paths reach the conservatory complex, but the Conservancy notes that some garden, green-space and bathroom routes have limitations. Contact the operator for a mobility-specific route rather than assuming every garden path is step-free.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.dogs: Pets are not allowed in Michigan state park buildings except service animals. Keep leashed pets in permitted outdoor areas and out of the conservatory.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.family: The indoor plant houses and adjacent aquarium make a useful weather-flexible pair, but children should remain on paths and adults should compare the two separate weekly schedules before arrival.
anna-scripps-whitcomb-conservatory.need: The conservatory is a staffed attraction, not an all-day extension of the park grounds. Arrive before 5:00 p.m., confirm holiday or event notices, and do not expect the aquarium to be open on Wednesday.

dossin-great-lakes-museum.description: Dossin Great Lakes Museum is Belle Isle's riverfront maritime museum, with the William Clay Ford pilot house, Miss Pepsi hydroplane, ship models and Great Lakes history exhibits.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.address: 100 Strand Drive, Belle Isle, Detroit, MI 48207
dossin-great-lakes-museum.location: Navigate to 100 Strand Drive and the named museum building on Belle Isle's south shore. It is separate from the Aquarium/Conservatory complex and requires its own island stop.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.parking: Use the lot directly adjacent to the museum off The Strand. Parking is free once the vehicle has a valid Recreation Passport or day pass; vehicle entry can pause when the island reaches capacity.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.hours: The museum is open Wednesday through Saturday, 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., and Sunday, 1:00-5:00 p.m. Special late openings, holidays and events can vary.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.restrooms: All museum bathrooms and water fountains are documented as wheelchair accessible, and baby-changing tables are available in multiple-toilet restrooms during museum hours.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.fees: Current general admission is $5 for adults and children, free for children under six and Detroit Historical Society members, with a $4-per-person household discount for five or more paid admissions. Vehicle entry still requires a Recreation Passport.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.accessibility: Accessible parking is north of the entrance, front-door drop-off is available, adult wheelchairs can be borrowed with ID, and the museum is stroller accessible. The William Clay Ford Pilot House is not wheelchair or stroller accessible.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.dogs: Only service animals should be expected inside the museum. Michigan DNR requires ordinary pets to remain leashed outdoors and prohibits them in state park buildings.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.family: Ship models, the hydroplane and pilot-house experience can work well for children. Baby-changing tables and sensory bags are available, but the pilot house is not stroller accessible.
dossin-great-lakes-museum.need: The museum has a paid ticket and a much shorter schedule than Belle Isle grounds. Summer vehicle capacity controls can stop cars at the bridge, so arrive early or use transit, bicycle or pedestrian access when the island is busy.

huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.description: Huron-Clinton Metroparks Water Garden is a 2.5-acre landscape of winding paths, wetland planting, seating, an open-air classroom, dock and bridge inside Ralph Wilson Park.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.location: Use the exact Water Garden pin in the eastern half of Ralph Wilson Park. It is distinct from seasonal Water Wonderland in the Play Garden; the Water Garden is a quiet ecological landscape, not a splash pad.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.parking: Use signed West Jefferson or Rosa Parks street parking, or walk from paid Bagley Mobility Hub via Southwest Greenway. Continue through the park to the Water Garden rather than stopping at the first playground entrance.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.hours: The outdoor Water Garden follows the park's daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. hours. Programs, ice, storms, flooding or maintenance can restrict the dock, bridge or individual paths.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.restrooms: Ralph Wilson Park lists public restrooms, with additional facilities at Bagley Mobility Hub. The operator does not promise a restroom inside the Water Garden itself, so confirm the nearest open park facility.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.fees: The Water Garden and ordinary park access are free. Parking in garages, food and selected programs may cost separately.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.accessibility: The new Water Garden includes winding developed paths, seating, a dock and bridge, but exact grades and weather conditions vary. Use the paved park approach and contact the operator when a specific accommodation is essential.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.dogs: Leashed, controlled pets are allowed in the park. Keep them on paths, out of the water and away from habitat plantings and environmental programs.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.family: The dock, bridge, wetland plants and outdoor classroom can support a quiet family nature stop. This is not Water Wonderland, and fishing is prohibited in the Water Garden.
huron-clinton-metroparks-water-garden.need: Do not confuse the Water Garden with the seasonal splash area. No fishing is allowed here; remain on paths and verify weather or maintenance status before relying on the dock or bridge.

william-davidson-sport-house.description: William Davidson Sport House is Ralph Wilson Park's open-air covered recreation pavilion with two full-size Detroit Pistons basketball courts and year-round programming.
william-davidson-sport-house.location: Use the exact Sport House pin near the middle of Ralph Wilson Park. The large circular-roof pavilion is separate from the Play Garden and Water Garden and should not inherit their operating hours.
william-davidson-sport-house.parking: Use signed West Jefferson or Rosa Parks street parking, Assembly Garage, or Bagley Mobility Hub via Southwest Greenway. Allow time to walk through the park to the covered pavilion.
william-davidson-sport-house.hours: William Davidson Sport House is open daily 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., two hours shorter than the surrounding park. Programs, court maintenance and events can control court availability within that window.
william-davidson-sport-house.restrooms: Ralph Wilson Park lists public restrooms, and Bagley Mobility Hub has additional facilities. Confirm the nearest open restroom rather than assuming one is inside the open-air court pavilion.
william-davidson-sport-house.fees: Ordinary Sport House and court use is free when available. Organized programming can use scheduled blocks, and parking or food may cost separately.
william-davidson-sport-house.accessibility: Paved park routes reach the covered Sport House and its hard court surfaces. Event setup and active play can affect circulation, so check the program schedule for a mobility-specific visit.
william-davidson-sport-house.dogs: Leashed pets may use ordinary park paths but should stay off active basketball courts and out of organized programs. Keep control around players and spectators.
william-davidson-sport-house.family: The covered courts support family recreation in more weather conditions than an uncovered court, but court availability is not guaranteed during programs. Bring appropriate footwear and supervise children around active games.
william-davidson-sport-house.need: The Sport House closes at 8:00 p.m., even though Ralph Wilson Park remains open until 10:00 p.m. Check the event calendar before promising an open court and yield to scheduled Conservancy programs.
